observations.body: The proverb places the king’s heart under the LORD, notes that people see their own ways as right, and says righteousness and justice are more acceptable than sacrifice.
observations.label: Justice is more acceptable than sacrifice

observations.body: The passage presents divine weighing, self-perception, righteousness, justice, and acceptance as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: divine weighing, self-perception, righteousness, justice, and acceptance

observations.body: The passage places justice priority beside divine weighing, self-perception, righteousness, justice, and acceptance.
observations.label: justice priority

payload.posture: Read Proverbs 21:1–3 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the comparison ranks moral action over sacrifice without supplying a full ritual critique
payload.title: Justice is more acceptable than sacrifice
